chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Earl Bostic, Tulsa High School and the broken clarinet
summary: Band director William Jett gives young Earl Bostic a clarinet, which Bostic's junk-dealer father breaks; Fields also notes Bostic subbing for Luther West.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: So I went on back then, when we did go back in Tulsa, we played those dates-- what's his name--Dorsey--had several dates and we played around and went back and Spurgeon was still going to school down in Xavier and I never would encourage him to stop school and I think Bostic had Scott around, Earl Bostic, and whenever I couldn't get Spurgeon I'd used
Yeah, Earl Bostic. And so I still liked Spurgeon better as a band man than lead sax, but boy, I tell you, Earl Bostic blowed more horn, he was just a genius. I felt really close to Bostic.

The band director there, William Jett, in Tulsa High School when it started, he was from Hampton University, Hampton and Tuskegee are very closely related and we got to be kind of buddy-buddy and run around together, and he used to say to me, I'm going to have a good man for you--talking about Bostic--in the high school band--and he gave Bostic a clarinet and his dad was a junk man. Bostic goes home and was practicing the clarinet and his old man came in one day and the boy was practicing there and he picked up the clarinet and broke it in two.

Yeah. He said my goodness, you're going to be blowing that thing around here, my son ain't going to be. And so from what I understand, the mother cried and everything and she called me and said you're a good friend of Mr. Jett, call him and tell him what happened, but I'll pay him for it.
So I told him and he said Ernie, you can tell her she won't have to pay one penny, I'll pay for it. That was the band director.
He said, she and everybody is going to be proud of that boy, the old man just don't know. He and I laughed about it. Here's a junk peddler talking about he don't want his
